questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The nitrogen atom in amines is:
questions.explanation: The nitrogen atom in amines is sp3 hybridized. It has three bond pairs and one lone pair, adopting a pyramidal geometry.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the nature of amines?
options: Amines are Lewis acids because nitrogen can donate electrons
Amines are both Lewis bases and Bronsted bases
Amines only act as Lewis acids
questions.explanation: Amines act as Lewis bases by donating the lone pair of nitrogen to acids, and as Bronsted bases by accepting protons from acids.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: When ammonium salt is treated with base, which type of amine is produced from primary ammonium salt?
questions.explanation: Treating a primary ammonium salt (RNH3+X-) with a strong base releases the primary amine (RNH2).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which compound, on treatment with NaNO2/HCl at 0°C followed by coupling with beta-naphthol, gives an orange-red dye?
questions.explanation: Aniline undergoes diazotization at 0-5°C, and the diazonium salt then couples with beta-naphthol to give an orange-red azo dye.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The reaction of alkyl amines with carbon disulfide (CS2) and subsequent treatment with mercury(II) chloride gives:
questions.explanation: Primary amines react with CS2 to form dithiocarbamic acid salts. On treatment with HgCl2, the product decomposes to give isothiocyanate (mustard oil). This is the mustard oil reaction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which property makes diazonium salts particularly useful in synthetic organic chemistry?
options: They are very stable at room temperature
The diazonium group can be replaced by a variety of groups
They are soluble in all organic solvents
questions.explanation: Diazonium salts are versatile synthetic intermediates because the -N2+ group can be replaced by -CN, -OH, -F, -Cl, -Br, -I, and -H, enabling synthesis of many substituted benzenes.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What is the role of Cu2Cl2 in the Sandmeyer reaction?
options: Reducing agent to convert ArCl to Ar
questions.explanation: In the Sandmeyer reaction, cuprous salts (Cu2Cl2, Cu2Br2, or CuCN) catalyze the replacement of the diazonium group with Cl, Br, or CN respectively.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Arrange the following based on increasing boiling points: (I) Butylamine (II) Diethylamine (III) Triethylamine
questions.explanation: Boiling points of amines depend on hydrogen bonding. Triethylamine (no N-H, no H-bonding) has the lowest bp, diethylamine (one N-H) is next, and butylamine (two N-H bonds) has the highest bp.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following aromatic compounds can best be synthesized using diazonium salts?
questions.explanation: Fluorobenzene cannot be made by direct halogenation (F2 reacts uncontrollably). The Balz-Schiemann reaction using diazonium tetrafluoroborate is the best route to fluorobenzene.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The coupling of diazonium salts occurs at which position of a phenol in alkaline medium?
questions.explanation: Coupling of diazonium salts with phenol (in alkaline medium) occurs preferentially at the para position to the -OH group because para-attack is sterically less hindered.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What is the key difference between aliphatic and aromatic diazonium salts?
options: Aliphatic diazonium salts are more stable
Aromatic diazonium salts are relatively stable due to resonance
questions.explanation: Aromatic diazonium salts are more stable than aliphatic ones because the positive charge is delocalized into the aromatic ring by resonance. Aliphatic diazonium salts decompose instantaneously.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following compounds will give stearic (octadecanoic acid) upon alkaline hydrolysis?
options: Methyl octadecanoate hydrolysis gives stearic acid: Octadecanamide
questions.explanation: Amides hydrolyze to give carboxylic acids and ammonia. Octadecanamide on alkaline hydrolysis gives octadecanoic acid (stearic acid).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is used to convert primary amines to secondary amines selectively?
options: React with exactly one equivalent of alkyl halide and separate carefully
questions.explanation: Treating a primary amine with an acyl group (amide formation) followed by LiAlH4 reduction gives a secondary amine in a controlled, selective manner.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is a correct statement about the Carbylamine reaction?
options: It is given by all amines with CHCl3 and KOH
Only primary amines give foul-smelling isocyanides (carbylamines)
It can be used to prepare amides
questions.explanation: The carbylamine (isocyanide) test is specific to primary amines. They react with CHCl3 and KOH to form foul-smelling isocyanides (R-NC) as the product. Secondary and tertiary amines do not give this test.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which among the following reacts with HNO2 (NaNO2/HCl) to give nitrosamines?
questions.explanation: Secondary amines react with HNO2 to give N-nitrosamines (R2N-NO), which are yellow oily compounds.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The reaction of aniline with sulphuric acid on heating gives sulphanilic acid. The sulpho group (-SO3H) in this compound is at the:
questions.explanation: Sulphonation of aniline via anilinium sulphate (formed first) gives para-aminobenzenesulphonic acid (sulphanilic acid) because the para position is less hindered.
